units.name: APLAs
units.assessment: Can you name the three antiphospholipid antibodies that carry diagnostic weight, state the antigen each is directed against, and describe the proposed mechanisms - cell-surface signalling, complement activation, NETosis - by which they create a prothrombotic state?

lesson.title: Antiphospholipid syndrome in 2020: Is complement the key?
lesson.why: A university grand-rounds hour on how antiphospholipid antibodies actually cause disease, with complement activation as the organising thread.

drills.name: Is APS complement-mediated?
drills.title: Session 7: Antiphospholipid Antibodies: Is APS a Complement-Mediated Autoimmune Disorder?
drills.channel: Foundation for Women & Girls With Blood Disorders

drills.name: Antibody profiles and patient stratification
drills.title: Antiphospholipid antibodies as tools for antiphospholipid syndrome patient stratification

units.name: Diagnosis of APS
units.assessment: Can you state which clinical and laboratory findings must coexist before you call a patient antiphospholipid syndrome, and explain how the 2023 ACR/EULAR weighted-domain criteria differ from the older Sydney consensus criteria?

lesson.title: 2023 ACR/EULAR AntiPhospholipid Syndrome (APS) classification criteria
lesson.why: A full session on the 2023 ACR/EULAR classification criteria themselves - the entry criterion, the weighted clinical and laboratory domains, and the point threshold.

drills.name: Diagnostic reasoning in APS
drills.title: Deep Dive into Antiphospholipid Syndrome Diagnostics

units.name: Prevalence of APLAs and APS
units.assessment: Can you estimate how common antiphospholipid antibodies are in healthy adults, in patients with lupus, and among unselected patients presenting with venous thrombosis, and explain why a single positive test in an acutely ill patient is usually not antiphospholipid syndrome?

lesson.title: Antiphospholipid Syndrome Management: Current Evidence
lesson.why: A thrombosis-network talk that sets out how often antiphospholipid antibodies turn up without disease, why a single positive test during acute illness or infection usually reflects transient positivity, and what confirmation at twelve weeks and antibody profile add before anyone is labelled with the syndrome.

drills.name: APS at its most severe
drills.title: The Antiphospholipid Syndrome: TMAs & pregnancy - Dr Karen Breen

units.name: Laboratory testing of APS
units.assessment: Can you walk through the three steps of lupus anticoagulant testing - prolongation of a phospholipid-sensitive screen, failure to correct on mixing, and correction with excess phospholipid - and explain why heparin, DOACs, warfarin and acute-phase states make the result uninterpretable?

lesson.title: Antiphospholipid Syndrome | Lupus Anticoagulant Testing: Fundamental Principles and Limitations
lesson.why: A thrombosis-network lecture devoted to lupus anticoagulant assay principles and, more usefully, to their limitations and interferences.

drills.name: Full laboratory workup for APLAs
drills.title: Laboratory Role in Diagnosis of Antiphospholipid Antibodies and Antiphospholipid Syndrome

drills.name: New antibody specificities and what testing adds
drills.title: Laura Bertolaccini - New specificities in the antiphospholipid syndrome - The importance of testing

units.name: Clinical consequences of APS
units.assessment: Can you list the thrombotic, obstetric and non-criteria manifestations of APS - livedo racemosa, valve disease, nephropathy, thrombocytopenia - and describe how catastrophic APS presents and what its combination therapy consists of?

lesson.title: The Antiphospholipid Syndrome - Dr. Michael Linenberger
lesson.why: A haematologist's full-length lecture on the clinical face of APS, running from venous and arterial events through pregnancy morbidity to the non-criteria manifestations.

drills.name: Microangiopathy and pregnancy manifestations
drills.title: The Antiphospholipid Syndrome: TMAs & pregnancy - Dr Karen Breen

units.name: Management
units.assessment: Can you justify why a vitamin K antagonist rather than a DOAC is used in triple-positive or arterial APS, cite the trial evidence behind that, and describe how chromogenic factor X is used when a lupus anticoagulant makes the INR unreliable?

lesson.title: Updates in Evidence in the Management of Antiphospholipid Syndrome (APS)
lesson.why: A long evidence-update session on APS management that covers the DOAC-versus-warfarin question, intensity of anticoagulation and what to do after breakthrough thrombosis.

drills.name: A haematologist talks through management
drills.title: #421 Antiphospholipid Syndrome with Dr. Arielle Langer

drills.name: DOACs vs VKAs in thrombotic APS
drills.title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants vs Vitamin-K Antagonists in Thrombotic Antiphospholipid Syndrome

drills.name: State-of-the-art management summary
drills.title: Antiphospholipid Syndrome: State of the Art Management | 24th ESR Annual Scientific Meeting

units.name: Special populations
units.assessment: Can you state the antithrombotic regimen for a pregnant patient with obstetric APS and no prior thrombosis, say how it changes for someone with previous thrombotic APS, and explain what happens to warfarin, aspirin and hydroxychloroquine across pregnancy?

lesson.title: Pregnancy and Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS)
lesson.why: A dedicated session on APS in pregnancy - who gets aspirin, who gets prophylactic versus therapeutic LMWH, and how refractory obstetric APS is approached.

drills.title: How we treat challenging cases of Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS)
